docs.text: Develop and publish the documentation ¶ Use a checkout of the source repository from its root. Install the extras in an active virtual environment . python -m pip install -e ".[dev,docs]" Preview and build ¶ The documentation includes a static build of the web demo . From the repository root, build the frontend and generate its fixtures first. Use the Python environment above and Node.js 24, which is also used in CI. npm ci --prefix web npm run build:demo --prefix web python examples/build_sample_demo.py docs/demo/data python -m mkdocs serve --strict Open 127.0.0.1:8000 . MkDocs reloads changes to the Markdown and navigation while the server runs. For the same strict build used in GitHub Actions, run this command. python -m mkdocs build --strict The build writes to site/ . Add pages through mkdocs.yml and link to relative Markdown paths in the source. The Python reference uses mkdocstrings directives that read signatures and docstrings from src/ . Update docstrings when the corresponding public contract changes and run new examples from an installed environment. Open the demo from the homepage. Regenerate its files after changing the dataset, supported settings, web interface, or Python result format. Run project checks ¶ python -m pytest python -m ruff check . python -m ruff format --check . python -m mypy src python -m build The examples directory contains runnable workflows for extraction, comparison, sweeps, temporal aggregation, reporting, experiment bundles, and plotting. From the checkout, run individual examples with Python, for instance python examples/parameter_sweep.py . If working on the frontend, CI uses Node.js 24. Use npm ci --prefix web to install frontend dependencies and npm run build --prefix web to build the packaged assets. Build assets only if working on the UI or preparing a package release. Publish the static site ¶ From a clean checkout of the revision to publish, follow the demo and site build steps above and review the generated site. Deploy the contents of site/ to a static host or use GitHub Pages. Set NETBONE_DOCS_SITE_URL to the public URL, including any path prefix, before building for publication. This sets the canonical URL and the links on the 404 page. For GitHub Pages, ensure the origin remote points to the publishing repository. Run these commands with credentials that can push to its gh-pages branch. Substitute your site's URL when publishing from a fork or to a custom domain. export NETBONE_DOCS_SITE_URL = https://al1yass2n.github.io/netbone/ python -m mkdocs gh-deploy --strict In PowerShell, set the variable with $env:NETBONE_DOCS_SITE_URL = "https://al1yass2n.github.io/netbone/" , then run the same MkDocs command. The command builds the site and pushes the generated files to gh-pages . For the first deployment, open Settings → Pages in the GitHub repository after the branch has been pushed. Select Deploy from a branch and set the source to gh-pages and /(root) . The CI documentation job verifies a build on pushes and pull requests. GitHub Pages deployment in MkDocs

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Installation and startup ¶ Symptom What to check Import works but nb.pipeline is missing Print netbone.__version__ and netbone.__file__ . Activate the intended environment and install from the current checkout . netbone-web is missing Check that the environment is active. Try python -m netbone.webapp --help to verify the package in that interpreter. The server reports an address-in-use error Pick a different port with --port , then open that port in the browser. The browser cannot connect Check that the terminal process is running and that the address and port match the startup message. Isolation Forest or plotting cannot import its dependency Install the ml or viz extra in the environment running Netbone. Input and scoring ¶ Symptom What to check Duplicate edge row For a static undirected edge list, A,B and B,A denote the same edge. Aggregate duplicate observations before loading or use the temporal loader for events. A weighted method rejects the graph Verify the selected weight attribute on each edge. Some methods require positive values or integer counts. See the method catalog . A method is incompatible with directed data Choose a directed-capable method or make an explicit undirected projection . Datetime events need a time setting Provide a snapshot_size for snapshot weightings or time_unit for persistent elapsed-time weightings. See temporal time scales . Results and downloads ¶ Symptom What to check A fraction retained more items than requested Netbone rounds the requested count up. The default policy also includes all cutoff ties. See fraction tie policies . All input nodes remain after edge filtering Edge filters preserve nodes by default. Use drop_isolates=True when only incident nodes should remain. A metric is missing Read status and explanation . Compatible topology is required for overlap. Constant ranks can make rank correlation undefined. A comparison or export no longer has its result Rerun the analysis after a server restart or cache eviction, then download the result again. Keep a ZIP for durable storage. The browser has counts but no graph drawing The live drawing is limited to networks of at most 80 nodes and 1,000 edges. Use graph export for larger networks. For a reproducible issue, include the Netbone version, Python version, method and filter settings, and a small representative graph. Remove sensitive data from anything you share.

docs.text: Compare, sweep, and export in the browser ¶ Compare saved backbones ¶ In the analysis view, filter a scored network and select Save this backbone . Change the method or filter settings and save a second result. To follow the browser tutorial , use two distinct retained fractions, such as 0.25 and 0.75. Open Compare , select the results, and run the comparison. Inspect single-result measures, pairwise overlap or score alignment. When values are unavailable, read the explanation in the result view. Download an individual table or chart, or use Export full experiment to save the comparison bundle. Overlap and ranking answer different questions. Two runs with identical scores and different cutoffs can agree on the ranks and still choose different edges. See reading comparison tables . Explore settings with a sweep ¶ Open Sweep from the analysis workspace. A sweep configuration names one method and one filter. You can add more configurations with independent method and filter choices. Mark the settings to vary and enter the candidate values for each setting. For example, with Keep a fraction , vary Retained fraction over 25%, 75% . Choose Review runs to inspect the combinations and select the run button to execute them. Each setup expands all combinations of its own varying settings. The browser allows at most 100 runs in a sweep. In Sweep results , choose a measurement, review the chart or table, and read the explanations for failed or unavailable values. Download run and metric CSV files, settings JSON, or the full experiment ZIP. Choose what to download ¶ Need Download Inspect an extracted graph GraphML or GEXF for the backbone or annotated original graph Rerun scoring and filtering Settings JSON plus the original input and its loading choices Analyze a comparison or sweep offline CSV for the measurements or a full experiment ZIP Keep a record of an analysis The full experiment ZIP, containing a manifest, deterministic Markdown and JSON reports, settings and tables, with graph exports for an extraction The preview and on-screen statistics may show a subset for larger networks. Use the exported tables and graphs when you need all rows. The reproducibility guide describes the bundle structure.

docs.text: Extract a backbone in the browser ¶ Try the web demo to compare two methods on a real network before installing the local app. Start the app , then use the built-in collaboration network to try extraction and export without preparing a file. Open Try an example and choose Weighted relationships . This example has four links with weights 4, 3, 2, and 1. If Review network settings opens, confirm that source and target are the endpoints and weight contains connection strengths. Choose Use this mapping . Select Choose method if the method picker is closed, then choose Edge Weight . If Compute scores is available, select it to finish scoring. In Choose a filter , select Keep a fraction . Set Retained fraction to 0.5. With these distinct weights, the two strongest links are retained. Check Network preview . Teal edges belong to the backbone and gray edges were left out. Backbone edges counts retained links. Node coverage counts nodes incident to those links, which can differ from the number of output nodes when the result retains isolates. Open Inspect & export . In Inspect , review the method statistics and open View run settings to download the pipeline JSON. Switch to Export for a GraphML or GEXF download. Backbone only is selected by default. Choose Download ZIP for the full experiment. Use Copy BibTeX in the app footer to copy the Netbone citation. Use Save this backbone to add the result to the current comparison list. To see how retention sensitivity affects the result, continue with comparison and sweep .

docs.text: Import a network in the browser ¶ Select Open a network or drag a file onto that button. Review the detected settings and the rows or graph summary before accepting the mapping. You can reopen the settings from the network summary. Input format Settings to verify CSV or TSV edge list Delimiter, source and target columns, optional weight, and direction. A static edge list represents one row per edge or arc. CSV or TSV temporal event list Select Temporal event list and map time and optional event magnitude as well as the endpoints. Choose a weighting and its timing parameters. GraphML Confirm graph direction and choose a numeric edge attribute if the analysis uses weights. Repeated static rows for the same edge are duplicates. Use a temporal event list if each row is a distinct time-stamped event. If a file carries weights, choose the appropriate numeric column and indicate whether larger values represent Strength or Distance . This choice guides path-based method settings. It does not change the imported values. Analyze directed inputs ¶ Declare source-to-target direction for directed edge and event lists. GraphML provides direction in the file. Keep orientation for a method that supports directed graphs. If you need an undirected method, the settings offer a projection. Choose how to merge weighted reciprocal arcs using sum, mean, maximum, or minimum. Use the method catalog to check direction and weight requirements. Aggregate events before scoring ¶ Select the temporal weighting, set the evaluation time when needed, and review the resulting static network. Repeated events aggregate per pair or per ordered arc. Check the temporal aggregation guide for snapshot size, elapsed-time units and magnitude rules. A method may be unavailable for the loaded graph or its selected attribute. Read the compatibility message under the method and correct the settings or choose a compatible method. The troubleshooting guide covers common failures.

docs.text: Run the local web app ¶ Install Netbone in your Python environment , then run either of these commands. netbone-web python -m netbone.webapp Open 127.0.0.1:8765 in a browser on the same machine. Keep the terminal open while you work. Press Ctrl+C there to stop the server. The installed distribution includes the browser assets. A separate frontend build is only needed when developing the UI. Startup options ¶ netbone-web --help lists both startup settings. Option Default Purpose --host 127.0.0.1 Address where the local server listens --port 8765 TCP port If the default port is occupied, choose another local port. netbone-web --port 8766 Then open 127.0.0.1:8766 . Where data is processed ¶ The browser sends the network to the local Python process for analysis. The server keeps recent scores, results and export handles in memory. Download files you want to retain before leaving the session. Restarting the server clears its caches. The supported setup is loopback on your own machine. The bundled server has no authentication or TLS and there is no supported hosted deployment. The app uses local HTTP routes for previews, analyses, and downloads. Their request formats and cached IDs belong to the browser implementation. Use the Python API for scripted analysis. Continue with the browser tutorial or import your own network .

docs.text: Method default ¶ Use default to apply the selection rule declared by a scoring method. Netbone reads the method's default filter and merges in any overrides you supply. The accepted arguments belong to the resolved filter. For example, a method that defaults to significance accepts alpha , while one that defaults to fraction accepts fraction . Some structural methods report membership flags. For these methods, the default filter extracts the marked edges directly. Others use a preset cutoff or fraction. Inspect nb.describe_method(name) and the method catalog to check which rule applies. A method without a registered default, such as Edge Weight, requires an explicit filter. Link Prediction requires direction even when using the default. result = nb . pipeline () . score ( "maximum_spanning_forest" ) . filter ( "default" ) . run ( graph ) Use the sample graph for this example.

docs.text: Fraction ¶ Use fraction for a retention budget on score, p-value, or numeric custom statistics. Give a number from 0 to 1. The requested count is ceil(fraction * number_of_rows) . A fraction of zero keeps zero items and a fraction of one keeps all items. The filter defaults to the primary statistic and the method's preferred direction. Override them with statistic and direction="higher" or direction="lower" . Link Prediction requires an explicit direction. Ties at the cutoff ¶ tie_policy Behavior include_all_ties (default) Keep every item tied at the cutoff. The realized count can exceed the requested count. exact_stable Break ties by internal ID and keep the requested count. raise_on_tie Raise an error if the cutoff splits a tie. random_seeded Choose the remaining items from the tied group using the required integer random_seed . Inspect the requested and actual counts in result.selection.parameters . Missing, non-numeric, or non-finite values cause a validation error. Use drop_isolates=True if you want an edge-target result without isolates. result = nb . filter_scores ( graph , scores , "fraction" , fraction = 0.5 , tie_policy = "exact_stable" ) Use graph and scores from the score reuse example .

docs.text: Significance ¶ Use significance with methods that report output_type="pvalue" . The filter selects rows whose adjusted p-value is strictly less than alpha (default 0.05). Both alpha and each p-value must be in the closed interval from 0 to 1. docs.text: Compare backbone results ¶ Run each candidate on the same input graph. If the question is which edges different methods prefer, start with a similar edge budget and check the achieved retention. For node-target methods, report node retention and edge retention separately. The example applies two cutoffs to the same collaboration network. One retains one edge and the other retains two. import networkx as nx import netbone as nb graph = nx . Graph () graph . add_weighted_edges_from ([( "A" , "B" , 8 ), ( "B" , "C" , 5 ), ( "C" , "D" , 2 )]) scores = nb . score ( graph , "edge_weight" , weight = "weight" ) results = { label : nb . filter_scores ( graph , scores , "threshold" , value = value , operator = "greater_equal" ) for label , value in { "strict" : 8 , "relaxed" : 5 } . items () } comparison = nb . compare ( results ) print ( comparison . table ( metrics = [ "edge_retention" , "connected_component_count" ])) print ( comparison . pairwise ( metrics = [ "edge_jaccard" ])) print ( comparison . spearman ()) The edge Jaccard value is 0.5 because one edge is shared out of two in the union. The score ranks agree because the two runs used the same scores. This illustrates how selections can differ even when the underlying ranks agree. Read the comparison tables ¶ table() measures each result. Use list_metrics(scope="single") to discover counts, node and edge retention, weight retention, and connectivity metrics. For directed results, use weak or strong component counts as appropriate. pairwise() measures overlap between results. Jaccard divides the intersection by the union. The overlap coefficient divides by the size of the smaller set. Overlap metrics require matching original topology. score_alignment(name_a, name_b) provides aligned statistics and importance ranks. spearman() measures rank agreement across result pairs. Both require the same attributed original graph and matching score targets. Constant ranks can make correlation undefined. In metric tables, inspect status and explanation before using value . An invalid row records an incompatible metric or comparison, and an undefined row records a metric that cannot be evaluated mathematically. Treat these rows as missing measurements. Plot a measurement ¶ Install the viz extra , then continue from the earlier example. The helper returns a Matplotlib axes. from netbone import viz ax = viz . plot_comparison_metric ( comparison , "edge_retention" ) ax . figure . savefig ( "edge-retention.png" , dpi = 160 , bbox_inches = "tight" ) Use plot_pairwise_metric(comparison, "edge_jaccard") for the corresponding pairwise chart. See the comparison API for additional table and plotting entry points.

docs.text: Prepare network inputs ¶ A Network is Netbone's validated representation of a simple graph. Its internal integer identifiers link graph elements to statistics rows. Use network.to_original_graph() or result.graph when you need the original node labels and input attributes. The input graph stays available as result.original_graph . Choose a loader ¶ Input Python entry point How weights and direction are handled CSV or TSV edge list nb.from_edgelist(path) Selected weight column becomes weight . Set weight=None for files without a weight column and delimiter="\t" for TSV. GraphML nb.from_graphml(path) Direction and node and edge attributes come from the file. Pass the chosen numeric attribute to the scoring method. NetworkX nb.from_graph(graph) A simple Graph or DiGraph is normalized. Scoring and pipeline execution also accept NetworkX graphs directly. Time-stamped rows nb.from_temporal_edgelist(path) Aggregate events into a weighted graph before running a pipeline. By default, static edge lists expect source , target , and weight columns. Pass their actual names as keyword arguments. A static file needs one row per edge. With directed=False , reverse rows belong to the same undirected edge and are rejected as duplicates. CSV input infers column types through pandas, so use string labels with a prefix if leading zeros are meaningful. GraphML or a NetworkX graph can represent isolated nodes explicitly. Preserve or project directed links ¶ Use directed=True for a CSV containing source-to-target arcs. A directed file can contain both A → B and B → A . Check the method catalog for directed support. If orientation can be discarded for your question, project explicitly and record the merge rule for reciprocal weights. import networkx as nx import netbone as nb flows = nx . DiGraph () flows . add_weighted_edges_from ([( "north" , "south" , 4 ), ( "south" , "north" , 3 )]) projected = nb . to_undirected ( flows , weight = "weight" , reciprocal_merge = "sum" ) assert projected . to_original_graph ()[ "north" ][ "south" ][ "weight" ] == 7 The merge choices are sum , mean , max , and min . Use weight=None, reciprocal_merge=None for unweighted projection. Reciprocal attribute conflicts are recorded as directional provenance. Parallel edges are unsupported. Most methods reject self-loops, so check compatibility before scoring data with loops. The input API reference contains the loader signatures.

Column mapping, direction conversion, and temporal aggregation happen before the pipeline runs. Export a self-contained record of the result ¶ This example saves a report, configuration and graph files in a temporary bundle. To keep the files, replace the temporary destination with a new directory of your choice. from pathlib import Path from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory import networkx as nx import netbone as nb graph = nx . Graph () graph . add_weighted_edges_from ([( "A" , "B" , 8 ), ( "B" , "C" , 5 ), ( "C" , "D" , 2 )]) pipeline = ( nb . pipeline () . score ( "edge_weight" , weight = "weight" ) . filter ( "threshold" , value = 5 , operator = "greater_equal" ) ) result = pipeline . run ( graph ) with TemporaryDirectory () as directory : bundle = nb . save_experiment ( result , Path ( directory ) / "collaboration-backbone" ) restored = nb . Pipeline . from_json ( bundle / "pipeline.json" ) . run ( graph ) assert set ( restored . graph . edges ()) == set ( result . graph . edges ()) print (( bundle / "manifest.json" ) . read_text ( encoding = "utf-8" )) The manifest lists the bundle schema, package and Python versions, subject type, and relative paths. Read report.md for the human-readable summary or report.json for a machine-readable report. docs.text: Choose what to keep ¶ Start with the reason for reducing the graph. If absolute connection strength matters, rank raw weights. If each node operates at a different scale, consider an endpoint-based method such as Disparity or LANS . For minimum connectivity within input components, start with a maximum spanning forest . The method catalog compares the input requirements and selection defaults. Match the filter to the statistic ¶ Analysis goal Filter What to specify Apply a numerical rule Threshold A cutoff and an explicit comparison operator Compare methods at a similar budget Fraction A retained fraction and, when it matters, a ranking direction and tie policy Use an output classified as a p-value Significance An alpha level and a multiple-testing correction Use a method's configured selection Default Any overrides required for that method A method reports target , output_type , primary_statistic , and preferred_direction . Small p-values are preferred. For a similarity score, the useful end of the scale depends on whether you want well-supported connections or structurally unusual ones. Use the primary statistic unless you have a specific secondary column in mind. An edge filter selects edge IDs. By default, the resulting graph keeps all input nodes, including isolates. Pass drop_isolates=True to omit nodes with no retained incident edge. A node filter selects node IDs and keeps every input edge between selected nodes. A node retention budget can therefore produce different edge retention rates on different graphs. Reuse an existing score table ¶ Score once when a method is expensive and you only need to change the filter. This example keeps the strongest two links and then keeps links above a cutoff from the same scores. import networkx as nx import netbone as nb graph = nx . Graph () graph . add_weighted_edges_from ([( "A" , "B" , 7 ), ( "B" , "C" , 4 ), ( "C" , "D" , 2 )]) scores = nb . score ( graph , "edge_weight" , weight = "weight" ) top = nb . filter_scores ( graph , scores , "fraction" , fraction = 0.5 ) cutoff = nb . filter_scores ( graph , scores , "threshold" , value = 5 , operator = "greater_equal" ) assert top . graph . number_of_edges () == 2 assert cutoff . graph . number_of_edges () == 1 Pass the same input graph or normalized network to both calls. Statistics contain internal IDs that identify rows in that input. Read result.warnings alongside the selection, particularly when ties or an uncorrected significance filter affect the interpretation. Apply a custom rule ¶ A custom filter receives a MethodResult , the input graph with original labels, and your keyword arguments. It must return a Selection for the same target, with IDs from the score table. The mask follows the table's row order. This filter computes its cutoff from the scores and delegates selection to a built-in helper. It uses graph from the previous example. from netbone.filters import apply_threshold def above_median ( method_result , original_graph ): column = method_result . primary_statistic return apply_threshold ( method_result , value = method_result . statistics [ column ] . median (), operator = "greater" , ) result = ( nb . pipeline () . score ( "edge_weight" , weight = "weight" ) . filter ( above_median ) . run ( graph ) ) assert result . graph . number_of_edges () == 1 Keep the callable in your Python source when sharing the workflow. The pipeline JSON format supports registered method and filter names.

docs.text: Find settings with a sweep ¶ Sweep a set of candidate settings when you need to see how an outcome changes over a range. Choose measurements that matter to the analysis. For example, edge retention quantifies the reduction while component count reveals fragmentation. import networkx as nx import netbone as nb graph = nx . Graph () graph . add_weighted_edges_from ( [( "A" , "B" , 8 ), ( "A" , "C" , 3 ), ( "B" , "C" , 5 ), ( "C" , "D" , 2 )] ) sweep_result = ( nb . sweep ( graph ) . score ( "edge_weight" , weight = "weight" ) . filter ( "threshold" , operator = "greater_equal" ) . vary_filter ( value = [ 2 , 3 , 5 , 8 ]) . measure ([ "edge_retention" , "connected_component_count" ]) . run () ) print ( sweep_result . table () . to_string ( index = False )) assert len ( sweep_result . runs ) == 4 assert sweep_result . score_cache_misses == 1 All four runs reuse one score computation. The lowest cutoff keeps all four links. The highest cutoff keeps only the link with weight eight. Vary a method or cross method and filter settings ¶ Use vary_method(...) when changing a method parameter with fixed filter settings. Use grid(methods=..., filters=...) for a Cartesian product of the entries. Mapping keys are registered names. A scalar is one value and a sequence expands into multiple candidates. To pass a list as a single parameter value, wrap it in an outer list, for example {"similarities": [["local_path", "shortest_path"]]} . grid = ( nb . sweep ( graph ) . grid ( methods = { "edge_weight" : { "weight" : "weight" }, "link_salience" : { "weight" : "weight" }, }, filters = { "fraction" : { "fraction" : [ 0.25 , 0.50 ], "tie_policy" : "exact_stable" }, }, ) . measure ([ "edge_retention" ]) . run () ) assert len ( grid . runs ) == 4 Different method settings have separate score computations. If a generated configuration fails, inspect failures for details. Successful runs remain available in results . Use runs for the configuration-level records and table() for the tidy measurement records. Inspect the status of a metric before using its value. With the optional plotting extra installed, use netbone.viz.plot_sweep_metric(sweep_result, "edge_retention") for the single-parameter example. For example, edge retention quantifies the reduction while component count reveals fragmentation. import networkx as nx import netbone as nb graph = nx . Graph () graph . add_weighted_edges_from ( [( "A" , "B" , 8 ), ( "A" , "C" , 3 ), ( "B" , "C" , 5 ), ( "C" , "D" , 2 )] ) sweep_result = ( nb . sweep ( graph ) . score ( "edge_weight" , weight = "weight" ) . filter ( "threshold" , operator = "greater_equal" ) . vary_filter ( value = [ 2 , 3 , 5 , 8 ]) . measure ([ "edge_retention" , "connected_component_count" ]) . run () ) print ( sweep_result . table () . to_string ( index = False )) assert len ( sweep_result . runs ) == 4 assert sweep_result . score_cache_misses == 1 All four runs reuse one score computation. The lowest cutoff keeps all four links. The highest cutoff keeps only the link with weight eight.

docs.text: Use vary_method(...) when changing a method parameter with fixed filter settings. Use grid(methods=..., filters=...) for a Cartesian product of the entries. Mapping keys are registered names. A scalar is one value and a sequence expands into multiple candidates. To pass a list as a single parameter value, wrap it in an outer list, for example {"similarities": [["local_path", "shortest_path"]]} . grid = ( nb . sweep ( graph ) . grid ( methods = { "edge_weight" : { "weight" : "weight" }, "link_salience" : { "weight" : "weight" }, }, filters = { "fraction" : { "fraction" : [ 0.25 , 0.50 ], "tie_policy" : "exact_stable" }, }, ) . measure ([ "edge_retention" ]) . run () ) assert len ( grid . runs ) == 4 Different method settings have separate score computations. If a generated configuration fails, inspect failures for details. Successful runs remain available in results . Use runs for the configuration-level records and table() for the tidy measurement records. Inspect the status of a metric before using its value. With the optional plotting extra installed, use netbone.viz.plot_sweep_metric(sweep_result, "edge_retention") for the single-parameter example. For auditing settings or results, see reproducing an analysis .

Aggregate temporal interactions ¶ Use a temporal edge list when rows are events rather than already aggregated edges. Repeated events for a pair are combined at an evaluation time. Each resulting edge weight is the sum of included event magnitudes multiplied by their temporal relevance. Apply a standard backbone method to the resulting static network. Choose the time scale ¶ Weighting Clock Parameters baseline Snapshots None. Sum event magnitudes. asf Snapshots p=3.0 sets the age scale, q=0.0 the long-run floor through q/(q+1) , and a=5.0 the sigmoid offset. persistent_exponential Elapsed time persistent_level in [0, 1] and non-negative decay_rate persistent_weibull Elapsed time persistent_level in [0, 1], positive scale and shape persistent_log_logistic Elapsed time persistent_level in [0, 1], positive scale and shape Use nb.describe_temporal_weighting(name) to see a weighting's formula and parameter constraints. Snapshot modes accept integer numeric snapshots. For raw numeric or datetime timestamps, bin with snapshot_size and optionally snapshot_origin . Datetime input requires a duration such as "1h" for snapshot size. Elapsed modes use exact age and accept time_unit to define its scale. With numeric time, the unit defaults to 1. For datetime input supply a duration such as "1d" . Persistent kernels take all their shape and decay parameters explicitly. Run a temporal analysis ¶ The example measures communications as of time 4. The late event at time 6 is excluded. Each reciprocal direction is aggregated independently. from pathlib import Path from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory import netbone as nb with TemporaryDirectory () as directory : path = Path ( directory ) / "events.csv" path . write_text ( "source,target,time,magnitude 
 A,B,0,2 
 A,B,2,1 
 B,A,2,3 
 B,C,3,2 
 A,C,6,1 
 " , encoding = "utf-8" , ) events = nb . from_temporal_edgelist ( path , event_weight = "magnitude" , directed = True ) static = nb . aggregate_temporal ( events , weighting = "persistent_exponential" , evaluation_time = 4 , persistent_level = 0.2 , decay_rate = 0.5 , ) graph = static . to_original_graph () assert graph . has_edge ( "A" , "B" ) and graph . has_edge ( "B" , "A" ) assert not graph . has_edge ( "A" , "C" ) result = nb . pipeline () . score ( "lans" ) . filter ( "significance" , alpha = 0.25 ) . run ( static ) print ( result . summary ()) The evaluation time defaults to the latest event. Omit the magnitude mapping to count each event with magnitude one. Self-interactions are removed, with their node labels retained. Aggregate zero-weight edges are dropped by default. Check network.metadata["temporal_aggregation"] on an aggregated network for resolved timing, event counts and the configuration. Persistent weightings also record persistent and transient contributions on the edges. Save aggregation settings via TemporalAggregationConfig.to_json() , then load them with TemporalAggregationConfig.from_json() and pass the config to aggregate_temporal(events, config) . Use the same events, column mapping, direction, and evaluation settings when rerunning the analysis.

docs.text: Networks and loaders ¶ Import these names from netbone . Use the loaders to create normalized networks and Network.to_original_graph() to obtain a NetworkX graph with input labels. Network dataclass ¶ A normalized NetworkX graph with stable internal node and edge ids. The stored graph uses integer node identifiers. Original node ids and edge attributes are preserved and result graphs are exported with original node ids. directed property ¶ Return whether the normalized graph is directed. edge_count property ¶ Return the number of edges in the normalized graph. multigraph property ¶ Return whether the normalized graph is a multigraph. node_count property ¶ Return the number of nodes in the normalized graph. weighted property ¶ Return whether any edge has a weight attribute. summary () ¶ Return a small JSON-compatible summary of the network. to_dict () ¶ Return a minimal JSON-compatible summary of this network. to_original_graph ( * , node_ids = None , edge_ids = None , drop_isolates = False ) ¶ Return a new NetworkX graph using original node ids. Parameters: Name Type Description Default node_ids Iterable [ int ] | None Optional internal node ids to include. When omitted, all nodes are eligible unless edge_ids and drop_isolates=True restrict them. None edge_ids Iterable [ int ] | None Optional internal edge ids to include. When omitted, all edges between included nodes are included. None drop_isolates bool Whether to omit nodes without retained incident edges. False Raises: Type Description ValidationError If unknown node or edge ids are requested. from_graph ( graph , * , context = None ) ¶ Normalize a simple NetworkX graph into a Network . Parameters: Name Type Description Default graph Graph A simple networkx.Graph or networkx.DiGraph . required context str | None Optional user-supplied context retained in result metadata. None Raises: Type Description CompatibilityError If the graph type is unsupported. ValidationError If reserved internal attributes are present. from_edgelist ( path , * , source = 'source' , target = 'target' , weight = 'weight' , delimiter = ',' , context = None , directed = False ) ¶ Load a CSV or delimiter-separated edge list into a Network . Parameters: Name Type Description Default path str | Path File path to read. required source str Column containing source node ids. 'source' target str Column containing target node ids. 'target' weight str | None Optional column containing numeric edge weights. When provided, values are stored on edges as the canonical weight attribute. 'weight' delimiter str Field delimiter, defaulting to comma. ',' context str | None Optional user-supplied context retained in result metadata. None directed bool Whether source-to-target order defines directed arcs. When false, reversed rows are duplicate undirected edges. False Raises: Type Description ValidationError If required columns are missing, ids are missing, edge weights are invalid, or duplicate simple-graph edges are present. from_graphml ( path , * , context = None ) ¶ Load a GraphML file into a validated Network . Parameters: Name Type Description Default path str | Path GraphML file path to read. required context str | None Optional user-supplied context retained in result metadata. None Raises: Type Description ValidationError If the file does not exist or cannot be parsed. CompatibilityError If the loaded graph type is unsupported by this release. to_undirected ( graph_or_network , * , weight , reciprocal_merge ) ¶ Return a deterministic undirected projection of a directed network. One-way arcs become undirected edges without changing their attributes. When both arc directions exist, the selected finite numeric weight is combined with reciprocal_merge . docs.text: Registry discovery and lower-level helpers ¶ Use the top-level registry functions to discover available methods and filters and inspect their metadata. For direct calls, the helpers shown below operate on normalized networks or computed method results. Most workflows can use netbone.score() , netbone.filter_scores() , or a pipeline. list_methods () ¶ Return registered built-in method names. describe_method ( name ) ¶ Return JSON-compatible metadata for a registered method. list_filters () ¶ Return registered built-in filter names. describe_filter ( name ) ¶ Return JSON-compatible metadata for a registered filter. Scorers exported by netbone.methods ¶ compute_disparity ( network , * , weight = 'weight' , pvalue_aggregation = 'min' , leaf_policy = 'ignore' ) ¶ Compute edge p-values from the disparity filter. For each endpoint of an edge, the method computes the fraction of that endpoint's strength carried by the edge, then evaluates the disparity null model p-value (1 - fraction) ** (degree - 1) . Endpoint p-values are combined into the method-specific primary statistic disparity_pvalue . For a directed arc, the source value uses its outgoing distribution and the target value uses its incoming distribution. Parameters: Name Type Description Default network Network Normalized simple directed or undirected network to score. required weight str Edge attribute containing finite positive weights. 'weight' pvalue_aggregation str How to combine endpoint p-values: min , max , or average . 'min' leaf_policy str How degree-one endpoints contribute: ignore ignores them during aggregation when another endpoint is available, while zero uses the previous behavior where leaf endpoint p-values are 0.0 . 'ignore' Raises: Type Description ConfigurationError If a method parameter value is invalid. ValidationError If a required weight is missing, non-numeric, non-finite, zero, or negative. compute_edge_weight ( network , * , weight = None ) ¶ Compute one edge score per edge from a numeric weight attribute. Parameters: Name Type Description Default network Network Normalized network to score. required weight str | None Edge attribute containing numeric weights. When omitted, every edge receives score 1.0 . None Raises: Type Description ValidationError If a requested weight attribute is missing or not finite numeric. compute_lans ( network , * , weight = 'weight' , pvalue_aggregation = 'min' , leaf_policy = 'zero' ) ¶ Compute LANS empirical upper-tail p-values for each edge. For undirected graphs, LANS compares an edge's fractional incident weight at both endpoints and combines the endpoint p-values. For directed graphs, each arc is evaluated only against its source node's outgoing fractional weight distribution; its source p-value is the primary lans_pvalue . Parameters: Name Type Description Default network Network Normalized simple graph to score. required weight str Edge attribute containing finite positive weights. 'weight' pvalue_aggregation str How to combine endpoint p-values: min , max , or average . 'min' leaf_policy str How degree-one endpoints contribute: zero treats the leaf endpoint as locally significant, while ignore ignores them during aggregation when another endpoint is available. 'zero' Raises: Type Description ConfigurationError If a method parameter value is invalid. ValidationError If a required weight is missing, non-numeric, non-finite, zero, or negative. compute_link_salience ( network , * , weight = 'weight' , distance_transform = 'inverse' ) ¶ Compute edge link salience from shortest-path trees rooted at each node. Link salience is the fraction of root nodes whose shortest-path tree or shortest-path directed acyclic graph contains an edge. The default distance_transform="inverse" treats input weights as coupling strengths and uses 1 / weight as the shortest-path distance. Parameters: Name Type Description Default network Network Normalized simple graph to score. Directed graphs use outgoing shortest paths from each root and preserve arc direction. required weight str | None Edge attribute containing numeric weights. Pass None for unweighted unit-distance salience. 'weight' distance_transform str inverse for strength weights or identity when weights are already shortest-path distances. 'inverse' Raises: Type Description ConfigurationError If distance_transform is unknown. ValidationError If a configured weight is missing, non-numeric, non-finite, non-positive for inverse , or negative for identity . Filters exported by netbone.filters ¶ apply_threshold ( method_result , * , statistic = None , value , operator , drop_isolates = False ) ¶ Select rows from method statistics using an explicit threshold operator. Parameters: Name Type Description Default method_result MethodResult Method statistics to filter. required statistic str | None Optional statistic column to compare. When omitted, the method result's primary statistic is used. None value object Numeric threshold value. required operator str One of greater , greater_equal , less , less_equal , equal , or not_equal . required drop_isolates bool Whether edge extraction should remove isolated nodes after filtering. False Raises: Type Description ConfigurationError If the statistic or operator is invalid. ValidationError If the threshold value or statistic values are not numeric. apply_fraction ( method_result , * , fraction , statistic = None , direction = None , tie_policy = 'include_all_ties' , random_seed = None , drop_isolates = False ) ¶ Select the top retained fraction of method statistics. The method result's preferred_direction controls the ordering. Lower values are preferred for p-values and higher values are preferred for ordinary scores. Parameters: Name Type Description Default method_result MethodResult Method statistics to filter. required fraction object Requested retained fraction in the closed interval [0, 1]. required statistic str | None Optional statistic column. Defaults to the method result's primary statistic. None direction str | None Optional ranking direction override. When omitted, the method result's preferred direction is used unless the method requires explicit direction. None tie_policy str One of include_all_ties , exact_stable , raise_on_tie , or random_seeded . 'include_all_ties' random_seed object | None Required integer seed when tie_policy="random_seeded" . None drop_isolates bool Whether edge extraction should remove isolated nodes after filtering. False Raises: Type Description ConfigurationError If the tie policy or statistic is invalid. ValidationError If the fraction or statistic values are invalid. apply_significance ( method_result , * , alpha = 0.05 , statistic = None , correction = 'none' , drop_isolates = False ) ¶ Select method rows whose p-values are significant. Parameters: Name Type Description Default method_result MethodResult Method statistics with output_type="pvalue" . required alpha object Significance level in the closed interval [0, 1]. 0.05 statistic str | None Optional p-value column. Defaults to the primary statistic. None correction str | None Multiple-testing correction: none , bonferroni , holm , or fdr_bh . 'none' drop_isolates bool Whether edge extraction should remove isolated nodes after filtering. False Raises: Type Description ConfigurationError If the method output or correction is incompatible. ValidationError If alpha or p-values are invalid. Version ¶ Read netbone.__version__ to record the imported package version.

Extract your first backbone ¶ You have a network of collaboration counts between teams. Keep the links supported by at least three collaborations, then check how much of the network survived. This tutorial uses a temporary CSV and runs after a core installation . Save and run this as a Python script. from pathlib import Path from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory import netbone as nb with TemporaryDirectory () as directory : path = Path ( directory ) / "collaborations.csv" path . write_text ( "source,target,collaborations 
 " "design,engineering,8 
 " "design,research,2 
 " "engineering,research,5 
 " "research,support,1 
 " , encoding = "utf-8" , ) network = nb . from_edgelist ( path , weight = "collaborations" ) scores = nb . score ( network , "edge_weight" , weight = "weight" ) result = nb . filter_scores ( network , scores , "threshold" , value = 3 , operator = "greater_equal" ) print ( scores . statistics [[ "source" , "target" , "score" ]] . to_string ( index = False )) print ( f "Retained { result . edge_fraction : .0% } of the edges." ) print ( "Isolates:" , sorted ( node for node , degree in result . graph . degree () if degree == 0 ) ) assert result . graph . number_of_edges () == 2 assert result . original_graph . number_of_edges () == 4 The score table contains four rows. The two retained links are design–engineering and engineering–research , so edge retention is 50%. support remains in the result as an isolated node. The CSV column named collaborations becomes the edge attribute weight when loaded. Save the choices as a pipeline ¶ Use a pipeline when you want to run the same method and filter again. The following uses network from the first example. pipeline = ( nb . pipeline () . score ( "edge_weight" , weight = "weight" ) . filter ( "threshold" , value = 3 , operator = "greater_equal" , drop_isolates = True ) ) result = pipeline . run ( network ) assert "support" not in result . graph compute(network) runs only the method. run(network) also applies the filter and constructs the resulting graph. For further exploration, see how to reuse a score table or compare two backbone configurations .

docs.text: Install Netbone ¶ Use Python 3.11 or later. The distribution and import are both named netbone . The core dependencies are NetworkX and pandas. These instructions target the 0.3.0 source tree. Install from a checkout to get the pipeline API and local web app described here. The 0.2.3 PyPI release belongs to the earlier GitLab codebase. Install from source ¶ Clone the GitHub repository and run the following from its root. python -m venv .venv Activate the environment for your shell. Shell Activation command PowerShell .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 Bash or Zsh source .venv/bin/activate Command Prompt .venv\Scripts\activate.bat python -m pip install . python -c "import netbone; print(netbone.__version__)" You should see 0.3.0 when installing this version of the source tree. The browser app is included in this install. Optional tools ¶ Run the command for the extra you need from the same checkout. Extra Install command Provides viz python -m pip install ".[viz]" Matplotlib plotting helpers ml python -m pip install ".[ml]" scikit-learn for Link Prediction Isolation Forest dev python -m pip install -e ".[dev]" Development and validation tools docs python -m pip install -e ".[docs]" The documentation builder and Python API handler Continue with your first Python backbone or launch the browser app .
